title: Constant-coefficient tower transport and prescribed scalar-associator normalization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, unital maps $A\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\xrightarrow{\psi}C$ of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and a morphism of schemes $q:Z\to Y$. Use the small pro-etale sites, their constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and the geometric operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $u=q_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For $R=A,B,C$ let $c_R:u^{-1}R_Y\to R_Z$ be precisely the map adjoint to constant sections [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Write $T_T^{R,S}=(-)\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ and $\alpha_{T,N}:T_T^{B,C}T_T^{A,B}N\xrightarrow{\sim}T_T^{A,C}N$ for the specified functors and associator of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Let $\tau_T$ be the balanced associator of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], for the tower of constant rings on $T=Y,Z$.

The maps $c_R$ are isomorphisms, and they identify the entire inverse-image coefficient diagram with the actual constant-ring diagram on $Z$:
$$c_B\circ u^{-1}(\varphi_Y)=\varphi_Z\circ c_A,\qquad c_C\circ u^{-1}(\psi_Y)=\psi_Z\circ c_B.$$
Under transport along these specified ring isomorphisms, scalar extension and the geometric module actions are the identified-coefficient operations just named. On either site, for every unbounded $N\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the resulting $\tau_{T,N}$ equals $\alpha_{T,N}$ as a morphism in $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},C)$. On any flat-term K-flat representative $P\to N$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], both successive and direct extension are computed by the same representative tensor complexes, and this common map and its inverse are
$$(P\otimes_{A_T}B_T)\otimes_{B_T}C_T\longrightarrow P\otimes_{A_T}C_T,\quad (x\otimes b)\otimes c\longmapsto x\otimes\psi(b)c,\qquad x\otimes c\longmapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes c.$$
These identifications are natural in $N$ and the coefficient maps, retain the right-factor $C_T$-action, and require neither flatness nor finite projective dimension of the ring maps nor boundedness of $N$.

proof.text: Use the already proved arbitrary-ring instance proEtaleConstantRingComparison_isIso for the specified adjunct c_R. Both constant coefficient squares follow by applying the sheafification adjunction to the direct-image maps, using naturality of toSheafify on constant generators, and then naturality of the inverse-image adjunction. This includes the empty site.

Apply the normalized scalar-extension-along-ring-isomorphism theorem. Connect changeOfRings to its independent-universe version by the presheaf identity isomorphism; its restrictions agree on pure tensors and sheafification preserves that isomorphism. The resulting comparison sends s tensor x to c inverse(s) times x, and its inverse inserts one. Whiskering with module inverse image proves geometric transport. The direct-image coefficient map is rho because homEquiv applied to its inverse recovers rho.

For any recorded Presentation family, reconstruct the full Normalization using the proved ordinaryComp, derivedComp, normalized adjunction data, representative and coherence lemmas of successive normalization. For a commuting coefficient square with vertical ring isomorphisms, paste inverse vertical extension, the first ordinary associator, equality of the composite ring map, the second inverse associator, and the source vertical relabelling. The ordinary_hom and ordinary_inv equations give s tensor x mapped to c_B(s) tensor x and the stated inverse. Naturality of the adjunction unit supplies naturality on pure tensors.

Restriction along each inverse ring isomorphism is an additive equivalence: construct it by pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence for the identity site equivalence. Apply the already proved leftDerivedSquare of ExactEquivalenceDerivedSquares to these two equivalences and the ordinary scalar square. complexCounitNat_kan transports each recorded universal homotopy counit to complex localization. The theorem's universal factorization equation is exactly the displayed counit equation for every unbounded complex; no resolving representative or K-flat assumption is required here.

Specialize the constructed Normalization to publishedPresentation on each pro-etale site, retaining every computation, representative, unit, naturality and associativity field. Its derived comparison is derivedComp for the published adjunction data. The already proved normalizedScalarComp_eq and publishedComp_eq identify the prescribed scalarExtensionFunctor_composition with that same derivedComp followed by equality transport of the coefficient map. Evaluating this natural-isomorphism equality proves the required equation at every derived object.

lean.statement: theorem proEtaleCoefficientTowerNormalization (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Finite A] [Finite B] [Finite C] (_hA : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a : A, (ℓ ^ n) • a = 0) (_hB : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ b : B, (ℓ ^ n) • b = 0) (_hC : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ c : C, (ℓ ^ n) • c = 0) (φ : A →+* B) (ψ : B →+* C) {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (q : Z ⟶ Y) : IsIso (proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap q A) ∧ IsIso (proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap q B) ∧ IsIso (proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap q C) ∧ (proEtaleSheafInverseImage q CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map (proEtaleConstantRingMap (T := Y) φ) ≫ proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap q B = proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap q A ≫ proEtaleConstantRingMap (T := Z) φ ∧ (proEtaleSheafInverseImage q CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map (proEtaleConstantRingMap (T := Y) ψ) ≫ proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap q C = proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap q B ≫ proEtaleConstantRingMap (T := Z) ψ ∧ (∀ T : Scheme.{u}, T = Y ∨ T = Z → ∃ ν : CoefficientTowerNormalizationData T, ∀ N : proEtaleDerivedCategory T A, (coefficientTowerBalancedComparison T ν (proEtaleConstantRingMap (T := T) φ) (proEtaleConstantRingMap (T := T) ψ)).hom.app N ≫ eqToHom (congrArg (fun a : proEtaleConstantRing T A ⟶ proEtaleConstantRing T C ↦ (reductionDerivedChange T a).obj N) (scalarExtensionFunctor_ringMap_comp φ ψ T)) = (scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ T).hom.app N)
